lines: Light a match on Earth, and the flame stretches up.
Hot air rises... and pulls fresh air in behind it.
Nothing rises. The flame turns round, and blue...
and it lives or dies on one thing: the air moving past it.
NASA has studied fire in space for decades.
But the answers are buried in test tables and long reports.
So we asked: what if an eight-year-old could investigate those real experiments... like a detective?
You start in Mission Freefall. Flip gravity off... and watch the flame change right in front of you.
Then you build NASA's real wind tunnel, piece by piece.
A crew of guides walks you through it. And PIX, our little evidence robot, gives you a hint whenever you're stuck.
Every chapter has one real job to do.
This is a real NASA film.
Switch on AI vision, and the computer outlines the flame and measures it, in pixels.
No made-up numbers. And we tell you it's an estimate.
Now, a detective game. Which outline really matches this NASA photo?
Get it right... and a clue lights up. Your explorer rank goes up, too.
Start with test B20. Turn the airflow down.
The atlas finds the real experiment, test B16... but it hides what happened.
So you have to predict first.
Then NASA's own words appear, with the exact page they came from. That's how real science works.
NASA has proposed thirty-four percent oxygen, at fifty-six and a half kilopascals, for future habitats.
So which real test is the closest clue? Pick one...
and you discover something big. None of our tests match.
And a missing test doesn't mean safe. It means a question nobody has answered yet.
A gap is a question, not a promise
You can ask PIX anything, and every answer links back to NASA's evidence.
And at the end, you don't get a generic score.
You get a list of exactly what you did... and a certificate with your name on it.
And for mentors and judges, the full science is right underneath.
Fifty-six tests from NASA's BASS-II report, each linked to its page.
Thirty-three NASA findings, each quote checked word for word against its source.
A mission planner, and an honest map of where the evidence runs out.
Real NASA data. A real adventure. And honest answers about what we still don't know.
